title: cycle record
description:
One run of any self-correcting agent loop, in ANY repo. This document is
the formal, machine-readable shape of the contract implemented by
~/.claude/hooks/cycle_telemetry.py. That module's validate_cycle() is the
actual enforcement (it also checks cross-field rules a plain JSON Schema
cannot express cleanly -- e.g. 'ended_at must not precede started_at',
'caught_by/missed_by must be empty when plant_id is null', 'a cost of
source unavailable must carry a reason' -- see that module's docstrings
for the authoritative list). This file exists so the shape is readable
and toolable without importing Python. Neither this file nor the module
names a repo, a product, or a specific loop -- 'system' and 'repo' are
opaque data supplied by whoever emits a record.

SCHEMA v2 IS PURELY ADDITIVE OVER v1: a schema_version:1 record with none
of the ten optional top-level arrays below (runs/reviews/changes/
decisions/issues_filed/evidence/corrections/verdicts/stages/
calibration_runs) still validates, forever, unchanged. The original nine
were built to close eleven measured completeness gaps against a real
session -- see ~/.claude/plans/cycle_log_schema_v2_gaps.md and
cycle_telemetry.py's own module docstring for the full rationale per
array. calibration_runs was added later (2026-08-29, GH #4648) under this
same additive contract, to express a grader-calibration GRID (many plant
AND clean-control rows in one record) the single `calibration` block
below cannot. schema_version is descriptive metadata (which shape a
record was AUTHORED against), not a gate on which optional keys may be
present -- a schema_version:1 record may carry v2 arrays too, since every
one of them is optional either way.

system.description: Slug identifying which loop this is, e.g. 'estimate-loop'. Never hardcoded by the runtime -- purely caller-supplied data.

repo.description: Repo NAME (not a path) that produced this cycle, or null.

ended_at.description: null means the cycle is still in progress.

runs.description: v2, optional. EVERY agent run this cycle made, not just the finder pass dispatches[] already models -- a run that found nothing still happened and still cost money.

reviews.description: v2, optional. Code/plan review boundaries -- v1 had NO review record at all.

changes.description: v2, optional. What actually changed as a result of a finding -- commit SHA (or 'uncommitted'), files, falsifiability evidence, tests added.

decisions.description: v2, optional. Who decided what and why, verbatim -- an OPERATOR ruling is first-class data here, never a note in prose.

issues_filed.description: v2, optional. Tracker issues filed as a result of this cycle.

evidence.description: v2, optional. File:line citations and repro commands raisers/verifiers actually used.

corrections.description: v2, optional. The loop's own error record -- a retraction of a prior claim.

verdicts.description: v2, optional. Raw per-scenario CONCUR/DISSENT verdicts before consolidation collapses them into findings[].

stages.description: v2, optional. Which pipeline stages ran/were skipped/were blocked this cycle, and why.

calibration_runs.description: v2, optional (added 2026-08-29, GH #4648). The GRID form of the `calibration` object above -- expresses a plants-x-trades grader-calibration grid (many plant AND clean-control rows in one record), which a single `calibration` object cannot. Never replaces `calibration`; both may be present independently, and neither is required by the other.

undispatched_verdict_rows.description: v2, optional (added 2026-09-07, round-25 structural-conflict fix). Honest accounting for a verdict row EXCLUDED from `dispatches[]` because it carries no real dispatch identity (e.g. a GC consolidation pass judging many scenarios within one already-open turn, never its own separate Task dispatch -- fabricating an identity for it is forbidden). `dispatches[]` holds real dispatches only; every excluded row's verdict still appears in `verdicts[]`/`findings[]`, unchanged -- this object is where the honest count of what got excluded, and by which judge, is recorded.

tokens_total.description: Harness-reported figure. NOT authoritative billed spend -- see cost.source and the README's 'why cost.source matters' section. The maximum is sys.float_info.max (round 16): cycle_telemetry.py's validate_cycle() refuses, at write time, an integer too large to survive a finite float conversion -- see is_finite_number()'s docstring. This bound is deliberately a hair STRICTER than the code's real acceptance boundary (int(sys.float_info.max) + 1 is still accepted there, because it rounds down on conversion); JSON Schema does not try to encode that float-rounding edge case, it just uses the clean, well-known constant.

cost_usd.description: The maximum is sys.float_info.max -- see tokens_total's description above for why.

tool_calls.description: The maximum is sys.float_info.max -- see tokens_total's description above for why.

duration_ms.description: The maximum is sys.float_info.max -- see tokens_total's description above for why.

batch_size.description: The maximum is sys.float_info.max -- see tokens_total's description above for why.

batch_position.description: The maximum is sys.float_info.max -- see tokens_total's description above for why.

tokens_reported.description: v2, optional. The harness's own (possibly untrustworthy) token figure, RECORDED rather than deleted -- requires tokens_source to be set whenever this is non-null. The maximum is sys.float_info.max -- see tokens_total's description above for why.

tokens_source.description: v2, optional. Provenance label for tokens_reported. Required (non-null) whenever tokens_reported is set.

tool_use_id.description: v2, optional. The spend ledger's own tool_use_id for this dispatch -- the STRONGEST identity signal resolve_cost() can match on (genuinely cycle-unique: one dispatch, one tool call). An empty string is a data defect (rejected), never treated the same as null/absent.

agent_id.description: v2, optional. The spend ledger's own agent_id for this dispatch -- an identity signal resolve_cost() can match on when tool_use_id is unavailable. An empty string is a data defect (rejected), never treated the same as null/absent.

session.description: v2, optional. The spend ledger's own session identifier for this dispatch -- the COARSEST identity signal resolve_cost() accepts; it establishes only same-SESSION correspondence, not same-cycle correspondence (a session can run more than one cycle). An empty string is a data defect (rejected), never treated the same as null/absent.

item_key.description: v2, optional. Renamed from wave_item (THE ISSUE WHEEL rollout, commit 8c) -- originally added for the retired Standing Delivery Wheel ('sdw' system), now a general-purpose field used by any system whose dispatches map to a discrete work item, e.g. THE ISSUE WHEEL's own lanes. A free-string join key back to a work item (conventionally the item's issue number as a string; 'row-<index>' for a fallback-mode item with no real issue number was the retired finishing loop's own convention -- THE ISSUE WHEEL's own ITEM TOKEN, schedules/prompts/issue_wheel.txt's LANE RECIPE, is issue-number-only, no fallback form). This is what makes a cycle's cost measurable PER ITEM, not just per cycle: tool_use_id/agent_id/session already let resolve_cost() find the right ledger row, but nothing before this field let a caller attribute that cost to a specific unit of work without re-deriving it from dispatch order. An empty string is a data defect (rejected), never treated the same as null/absent -- same convention as tool_use_id/agent_id/session.

scenarios.description: v2, optional. AA-0106 (2026-09-07). The individual units of work (e.g. scenario ids) ONE REAL DISPATCH actually covered, for a caller whose dispatch batches many scenarios into a single sub-agent call. The contract this field exists to enforce: exactly ONE dispatches[] entry per REAL Task dispatch, never one entry per scenario -- a producer that instead multiplied one dispatch into N synthetic entries (one per scenario, every one echoing the same tool_use_id) is the defect this field closes; resolve_cost()'s step-4a 1:1 identity check correctly refuses such a record outright. An empty array is a data defect (rejected), never treated the same as absent -- omit the key instead.

plant_id.description: null means no calibration plant was seeded this cycle.

caught_by.description: Slot identifiers (typically dispatches[].batch_position) that caught the plant.

missed_by.description: Slot identifiers that were exposed to the plant but did not report it.

calibration_run.description: One row of calibration_runs[] (v2, optional, added 2026-08-29, GH #4648). Cross-field rules enforced by the Python validator, not expressible cleanly here (same pattern as this file's other Python-only cross-field rules, e.g. `evidence` below): caught_by/missed_by must be empty when plant_id is null (a CONTROL row -- nothing was seeded to catch or miss); false_alarm_finding_ids must be empty when plant_id is not null (a PLANT row -- a finding against a genuinely-seeded plant is a catch/miss, never a false alarm). See cycle_telemetry.py's _validate_calibration_run for the authoritative enforcement.

plant_id.description: null means this row is a CLEAN CONTROL -- no plant was seeded in it.

batch_size.description: The maximum is sys.float_info.max -- see dispatch.tokens_total's description for why.

caught_by.description: Slot identifiers that caught the plant. Must be empty on a control row (plant_id null).

missed_by.description: Slot identifiers that were exposed to the plant but did not report it. Must be empty on a control row (plant_id null).

false_alarm_finding_ids.description: Blocker/DISSENT finding id(s) raised against this row's package. Must be empty on a plant row (plant_id not null) -- see this def's own description above.

undispatched_verdict_rows.description: v2, optional (added 2026-09-07, round-25 structural-conflict fix). Cross-field rule enforced by the Python validator, not expressible cleanly here (same pattern as `calibration_run` above): by_judge's values must sum to exactly count -- see cycle_telemetry.py's _validate_undispatched_verdict_rows for the authoritative enforcement.

count.description: Total number of verdict rows excluded from dispatches[] this cycle because they carried no real dispatch identity.

by_judge.description: Per-judge breakdown of the excluded count, keyed by the ledger's own raw judge label (e.g. "gc"). A TRADE judge appearing here (rather than only "gc") means that judge's dispatch identity was never recorded -- a recording miss, made visible here rather than silently absent from both dispatches[] and this accounting.

verifier_cause_upheld.description: Was the RAISER's stated root cause actually right? null means not yet judged.

fights_ruling.description: Truthy (a ruling id string, or true) means this finding contradicts an already-ratified ruling.

found_at_stage.description: v2, optional. Accepts a 'consolidation' origin so a finding the consolidator surfaced but that never reached a verifier is representable at all.

issue_refs.description: v2, optional. Issue id(s) filed as a direct result of this finding.

source.description: 'unavailable' extends the base 'spend_ledger|reported' pair for the honest-refusal path (see resolve_cost in cycle_telemetry.py) -- a real cost figure is never fabricated.

total_tokens.description: The maximum is sys.float_info.max -- see dispatch.tokens_total's description for why.

total_usd.description: The maximum is sys.float_info.max -- see dispatch.tokens_total's description for why.

reason.description: Required (by the Python validator, not expressible cleanly here) whenever source is 'unavailable', or when source is 'spend_ledger' with total_usd null.

tolerance_sec.description: The maximum is sys.float_info.max -- see dispatch.tokens_total's description for why.

outcome.description: Never empty, even for a run that found nothing -- e.g. 'occurred; no further detail captured' is a valid, honest outcome.

fixed.description: null means not yet re-confirmed -- never assumed true.

outcome.description: Cross-checked against blocker_count by the Python validator: 'clean' requires 0, 'blockers' requires >=1.

commit_sha.description: Literal string 'uncommitted' is valid when nothing has landed yet.

red_before_green.description: Falsifiability evidence text, or the literal 'unverified' when it genuinely wasn't done -- never omitted.

decided_by.description: A free string, e.g. an agent type OR the literal 'OPERATOR' -- operator rulings are first-class data, not a special enum value.

reasoning.description: Verbatim reasoning, required and non-empty -- this is the entire point of the array.

evidence.description: Cross-field rule enforced by the Python validator, not expressible in JSON Schema itself: at least one of file/quote/repro_command must be non-null.

blocked_reason.description: Required (by the Python validator) and non-empty whenever status is 'blocked'.
